## Crosshole tomography

```{python}
#| eval: true
#| echo: false

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pygimli as pg
```

For this example, we use the [traveltime module](https://www.pygimli.org/pygimliapi/_generated/pygimli.physics.traveltime/) from [pyGIMLi](https://www.pygimli.org)

```{python}
import pygimli.physics.traveltime as tt
```

```{python}
data = tt.createCrossholeData(x=[0, 10], z=-np.arange(10)-0.5)
```

We create a grid of
```{python}
x = np.arange(10.1)  # 0 1 .. 10
y = -np.arange(0, 12.1)  # 0 1 .. 11
grid = pg.createGrid(x, y)
print(grid)
pg.show(grid);
```

```{python}
ax, cb = grid.show(grid.cellMarkers(), showMesh=1,
                   colorBar=False, cMap="Spectral")
sx = pg.x(data)
sy = pg.y(data)
sC = data.sensorCount()
ax.plot(sx[:sC//2], sy[:sC//2], "b*", ms=8)
ax.plot(sx[sC//2:], sy[sC//2:], "gs", ms=8)
# ax.figure.savefig("crosshole-setup.svg")
for s, g in zip(data["s"], data["g"]):
    ax.plot([sx[s], sx[g]], [sy[s], sy[g]],
            color="0.8", alpha=0.5, lw=1)
```





## Smoothness constraints

```{python}
#| echo: false

nB = 9*9 + 10*8
C = np.zeros([nB, grid.cellCount()]) # 9x10
i = 0
for row in range(9):
    for col in range(9):
        left = row*10+col
        C[i, left] = -1
        C[i, left+1] = 1
        i += 1

for row in range(8):
    for col in range(10):
        up = row*10+col
        C[i, up] = -1
        C[i, up+10] = 1
        i += 1
```

```{python}
#| echo: true

plt.spy(C)
```
